findings.source_passage: they are so shut up, belted about, every way inclosed, surrounded, and made an utter island of by the ocean, that to their very chairs and tables small clams will sometimes be found adhering, as to the backs of sea turtles
findings.source_locator: second paragraph, closing sentence of the extravaganzas list
findings.why_it_matters: This is the rhetorical climax of the comic extravaganzas passage — the accumulation of synonyms ('shut up, belted about, every way inclosed, surrounded') and the image of clams adhering to chairs are distinctive voice-markers; their removal cuts the paragraph's punchline.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at minimum the clam-adhering-to-chairs image and the preceding accumulative synonyms; they are brief enough to include without blowing the word budget.

findings.source_passage: The Nantucketer, he alone resides and riots on the sea; he alone, in Bible language, goes down to it in ships
findings.why_it_matters: The draft drops 'he alone resides and riots on the sea' and collapses the anaphoric 'he alone … he alone' to a single instance, erasing the rhetorical amplification that gives the sentence its declamatory signature weight.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'The Nantucketer, he alone resides and riots on the sea; he alone, in Bible language, goes down to it in ships' as written.

findings.source_passage: he lives on the sea, as prairie cocks in the prairie; he hides among the waves, he climbs them as chamois hunters climb the Alps
findings.why_it_matters: These similes (prairie cocks, chamois hunters) are the rhythmic and imagistic peak of the Nantucketer apostrophe; they are entirely cut, leaving the closing paragraph with a flattened trajectory before the gull image.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the prairie-cocks and chamois-hunters similes between the Noah's flood sentence and 'For years he knows not the land.'

findings.source_passage: more strangely than the moon would to an Earthsman
findings.source_locator: final paragraph, 'when he comes to it at last' clause
findings.why_it_matters: The moon-Earthsman comparison is a distinctive Melvillean register marker; the draft's truncation to 'it smells like another world' strips the cosmic amplification.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'more strangely than the moon would to an Earthsman' after 'it smells like another world.'

findings.source_passage: Merchant ships are but extension bridges; armed ones but floating forts; even pirates and privateers, though following the sea as highwaymen the road, they but plunder other ships
findings.source_locator: final paragraph, after 'right of way through it'
findings.why_it_matters: This catalogue of maritime types (merchants, warships, pirates) defines Nantucketer supremacy by contrast and is part of the interpretive argument about sea-ownership; its removal weakens the conceptual architecture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the merchant-ships/armed-ones/pirates triptych as a compressed clause before 'He alone, in Bible language.'

summary: Three medium-severity findings — the clam/chairs climax of the extravaganzas passage, the dropped 'resides and riots'/'he alone' anaphora, and the absent prairie-cocks/chamois similes — collectively constitute voice erasure sufficient to require regeneration.
